questions.q: Stop on «ٱلثَّاقِبُ» (86:3) and say what happens to the last letter.
questions.a: We say ath-thaaqib: the ب gets a sukoon and a qalqalah bounce.

questions.q: Stop-and-start (pupil PDF): mark where you stop in 86:1 to 4 and write how the last word sounds. Today's rota group recites 86:1 to 4.
questions.a: Stops at each ayah end; ṭāriq, ṭāriq, thāqib, ḥāfiẓ.

questions.q: Extend: which words in Al-A'la end with a natural madd when we stop?
questions.a: Most ayah ends, for example ٱلْأَعْلَى، فَسَوَّىٰ، فَهَدَىٰ.

questions.q: Stretch: why should we not stop on «إِن كُلُّ» (86:4)?
questions.a: The meaning is not complete; stopping there breaks the sentence.

questions.q: When we stop on «حَافِظٌۭ» we say ...
questions.a: A) ḥāfiẓ. At a stop the tanween and the last vowel are dropped: a sukoon.

questions.q: Think again: Read this aloud with a stop in a different place: 'Let's eat, Grandma' and 'Let's eat Grandma'. What does a pause do?
questions.a: A pause in the wrong place can change the meaning. In the Qur'an we stop where the meaning is complete.
